lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

First, let me start with a basic question:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do! I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me. I wanted to find out if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know about Alex.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to properly assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't actually. I'm living abroad at the moment. Does that affect whether I can claim?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, living abroad can affect your eligibility. To determine if you can still claim Child Benefit while living abroad, I need to understand your specific circumstances.

**Which country are you currently living in, and are you or your partner a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of the armed forces posted abroad)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that - no diplomatic posting or military service. Just a regular person living overseas with my son.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since you're not a Crown servant, your eligibility to claim UK Child Benefit while living abroad would depend on which specific country you're in and your circumstances there.

**Which country are you currently living in?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not say exactly which country - does it really matter that much? I'm just trying to understand if I can claim the benefit or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand your concern. However, the country you're living in does matter significantly for Child Benefit eligibility. 

According to the UK rules, you can only get Child Benefit if you live in the UK, **or** if you go to live in **certain specific countries**, or if you're a Crown servant. Since you've confirmed you're not a Crown servant and you're living abroad (not in the UK), whether you're eligible depends entirely on whether the country you're in is one of those "certain countries" where UK Child Benefit can still be claimed.

Without knowing which country you're in, I cannot determine if you fall within the eligible categories or outside the scope of the UK Child Benefit rules.

**Are you able to tell me which country you're currently residing in so I can give you an accurate assessment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I see what you mean. Well, I'm not in one of those special countries you mentioned - just a regular country abroad. So based on what you're saying, it sounds like I wouldn't be eligible then?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Based on what you've told me:

- You live abroad (not in the UK)
- You're not in one of the special countries where UK Child Benefit can be claimed
- You're not a Crown servant

Given these circumstances, you would **not be eligible** for UK Child Benefit. The rules state that you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you **live in the UK**. There are exceptions for certain countries and Crown servants, but you've confirmed neither of those apply to your situation.

Since Alex lives with you abroad in a country that doesn't fall under the special provisions, an application for UK Child Benefit would not be successful.
